_about: Single source of truth for provider and model limits. Nothing here should be duplicated at a
call site: read it through core/provider.limits.js instead. Adding a model is one entry;
a vendor changing a number is a one-line edit that every caller picks up.
null means 'not established yet', never 'unlimited'. The accessor never invents a value, so a
null reaches the caller as null and the caller decides what to do about it.

groq: Every response carries x-ratelimit-* headers. Mind the windows, they differ:
x-ratelimit-limit-requests resets on a daily window (~24h), so it is requestsPerDay.
x-ratelimit-limit-tokens resets in well under a second, so it is tokensPerMinute.
Groq does publish a per-minute request cap but does not return it in a header; left null.
gemini: No rate-limit headers at all. The numbers come out of a 429 body:
error.details[].violations[].quotaId names the window, .quotaValue is the number.
openrouter: Responses carry x-ratelimit-limit / -remaining / -reset for the account, not the model.
Per-model context length: GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models, field context_length.

_maxRequestTokens: A single request is billed against the per-minute token budget, so one request can never
exceed tokensPerMinute however long you wait. Confirmed by 413s at 8529 tokens on
This is the number that decides whether a whole transcript can be prompted at all.
_tokensPerDay: A fourth window, and the one that stays invisible until it bites: no header reports it,
it only names itself in a 429 body as 'tokens per day (TPD)'.
It is per model and the models differ — gpt-oss-120b allows 200000, llama-3.3-70b-versatile
only 100000. Both were read off a 429 an hour apart. It was briefly recorded as a provider
default of 200000 on the strength of the first measurement, which made llama look twice as
affordable as it is; hence null here and a number only where one has actually been seen.

_note: Twenty per day, not per minute — quotaId GenerateRequestsPerDayPerProjectPerModel.
Accepted a 12109-token prompt, so context is not the constraint here, volume is.
Unusable for any batch job; an evaluation run exhausted it in sixteen calls.

gemini-2.0-flash._note: 429s immediately on this key; quota not yet read off a violation body.

_note: Two separate quotas, both read off 429 bodies:
The daily one is the tighter constraint in practice and is what one-request-per-chunk
spent: five meetings of a few hundred chunks each exhausted 1000 in an afternoon.
batchEmbedContents takes up to 100 per request (50 used, for headroom on long chunks),
which turns a 116-chunk meeting from 116 requests into 3.

_why: Far roomier than Groq on the same model: 1M tokens/day against 200k, 30k/min against 8k,
and a 65k context against an effective 8k per request. That last one is what decides
whether a whole transcript can be prompted at all.
The catch is requests, not tokens: 5 per minute. Fine for batch evaluation, too slow for
a live chat path, which is why production stays on Groq for latency and this is the
better home for long-context and bulk work.
Model ids differ from Groq's for the same model — 'gpt-oss-120b', not 'openai/gpt-oss-120b'.

zai-glm-4.7._note: preview model, may be withdrawn at short notice

_billing: Billed by AUDIO DURATION, not tokens — so the token fields here do not apply to it.
There is no usage endpoint: /v1/usage, /usage, /v1/me, /v1/account, /v1/credits and
/v1/quota all 404. The remaining balance is visible only on the Sarvam dashboard, so it
cannot be checked from code and has to be read there and written in below.
Known spend on batch STT: 3.49 hours of audio (209.6 min across 23 jobs) on 2026-08-09
for the evaluation corpus. Realtime-lane experiments before that are not accounted for.

_note: num_speakers is optional and the provider detects the count when it is omitted.
Eight is the ceiling, well under the thirty the live FunASR lane tracks, so batch
reconciliation cannot confirm speakers beyond the eighth.

_maxRequestTokens: OpenRouter routes to many upstream models, so the ceiling belongs to the model, not the
account. Add a models entry with the real number once a request has actually been sent.
Left null everywhere so a caller sees 'not established' rather than a guess.

stealth/ox-alpha._note: Free tier, cost 0 confirmed in a response body. context_length from GET /api/v1/models.
